why: I compared each verifier check's PASS and FAIL conditions with the words of its expect line. Check 1 passes when the call "does not throw on the invalid JSON" and returns `{}`. It fails on a throw, on a non-`{}` result, or when "the handling is not in loadConfig in src/config.js". The line names that location ("loadConfig(path) in src/config.js catches..."), so the location rule comes from the words, not from extra strictness. Check 2 passes when "the test run reports no failing tests" and fails if a test fails or the command errors out. That is just what "npm test passes" requires. The stricter items all sit under "Advisory (does not affect PASS/FAIL)": loading a valid file, missing-file read errors still throwing, the stderr message, exit status 0, replacing the old test, and the README and app behaviour. No PASS or FAIL condition goes beyond what its line's words require.
